rows.claim: Declared state/mode fields are selectively auto-published
rows.fix: Annotation: auto-publication was removed by D-252; a component exposes a state or mode field by returning it from y_state.
rows.note: D-252 (log.md:10447) removed auto-publishing. D-035's own rationale (log.md:1334) already says a field is exposed by returning it from y_state. _outputs takes a component's ports from keyed_outs alone. Failure: a component that declares a mode field gets no port for it unless its y_state returns it as a declared port.

rows.claim: Deployment binding happens at Simulation construction only
rows.fix: Annotation: deployment binding produces a Deployment artifact (D-254), which a Model materializes (D-317); Simulation(build; kw...) is sugar that composes the two.
rows.note: D-254 (log.md:10569) moved binding into the Deployment artifact, and D-317 split the Model out. bind_schedule runs in the Deployment constructor (deployment.jl:573), and Simulation(build; kw...) composes Deployment and Model (sim.jl:394-396). Failure: Deployment(build; Δt_frame) binds the schedule without any Simulation being constructed.

rows.claim: Handler-phase u gathers materialize at round start, after guards, before any handler
rows.fix: None beyond the 2026-10-02 annotation (log.md:3404): D-154 retired the materialization, and round-start u holds by construction.
rows.note: D-154 (log.md:6045) removed the mechanism. Only sweeps write the table, and a handler's bundle is gathered when it fires (executor.jl:394). The entry's own annotation records this. Failure: no round-start u buffer exists; make_handler_bundle gathers u from the live store at each firing.

rows.claim: The per-event re-decode reuses the round-start u
rows.fix: None beyond the 2026-10-02 annotation (log.md:3404): the per-event re-decode is gone (D-154).
rows.note: D-154 (log.md:6049) removed the per-event re-decode. The fire walk runs handlers and projections only, and the re-sweep is the next round's _round! (model.jl:773-775). Failure: after a handler fires, no stage re-decodes y before the next handler.

rows.claim: Same-component successors see refreshed own ports; handler returns latch per event
rows.fix: Annotation: a component fires at most one event per round (D-154), so no same-component successor runs within the round.
rows.note: D-154 serializes a component's events across rounds (model.jl:760-763, comp_fired). The 2026-10-02 annotation at log.md:3404 covers the mechanism but not this visibility clause. Failure: two events of one component that are eligible at once fire in successive rounds, the second after a re-sweep, never as a successor within one round.

rows.claim: log_max is a new Simulation keyword beside log/log_every
rows.fix: None beyond the 2026-10-13 annotation (log.md:5009): log_max is a keyword of init!, overlay!, restore! and replay! (D-261).
rows.note: D-261 moved the recording keywords to the calls that open a run, and the entry's annotation at log.md:5009 records it. Simulation(...; log_max) is refused (probe:151) and init!(...; log_max) is accepted (probe:152); see sim.jl:349-351. Failure: Simulation(Plant(); Δt_frame = 1//10, log_max = 10) throws a MethodError from Deployment.

rows.claim: A field-emitting component exposes a plain, pure, exported value-level constructor
rows.note: This is an authoring obligation on shipped components. No component in src/ or examples/ emits a field handle, so nothing in the code can meet or break it. atmospheric_field and SimpleAtmosphere are absent from src, test and examples.

rows.claim: The component's swept output stage is a one-line call to the constructor, never the reverse
rows.note: Same obligation as L6c-053. No shipped component emits a field handle, so there is nothing to check this against.

rows.claim: Every output stage returns its port NamedTuple alone
rows.fix: Annotation: under a bare y_types a stage returns the one port's value, not a NamedTuple (D-437).
rows.note: D-436/D-437 (log.md:17996, 18128) added the bare contract. build.jl:80-88 holds a named return to a NamedTuple and a bare return to the port's type. Failure: BareScale's y_direct returns -2.0 * u, a Float64, and the model builds (test/fixtures.jl:90, test_build.jl:1855).

rows.claim: An opaque leaf is accepted by identity alone
rows.fix: None beyond the 2026-09-25 annotation (log.md:9755): identity governs a store and the producer's own check, and at a wire a frozen opaque arrival is admitted at an unpinned entry (D-264).
rows.note: D-264 narrowed the rule. _accepts applies identity only when !at_wire (leaves.jl:355), and _accepts_wire admits the producer's cell (leaves.jl:370-375). Failure: a Pinned{Handle{Float64}} producer feeding an unpinned Handle{T} entry passes the wire relation by lift, not by identity.

rows.claim: The embedding lift never enters an opaque leaf
rows.fix: Annotation: at a wire the lift enters an opaque leaf (D-264); at a store it never does.
rows.note: D-264 narrowed the rule to stores. The docstring at leaves.jl:349-350 says at_wire lets the lift enter. Failure: _accepts(P, V, T, true) on an opaque P walks its parameters with the lift.

rows.claim: StopRequest has a Bool input `request` and a StopFlag output `flag`
rows.fix: Annotation: StopRequest's contracts are bare since D-436/D-437, its Bool input the face u and its StopFlag output the face y.
rows.note: D-436 (log.md:18050) made the single-port blocks bare, and D-437 (log.md:18188) names a bare StopFlag requester's port y. The 2026-11-12 annotation (log.md:14492) says the spelling and the rest stand, which is wrong for the port names. Leads: request, flag (test-only). Failure: u_types(StopRequest()) is Bool and y_types is StopFlag (probe:111), and the roster entry is Requester("r", :y, "why") (probe:109).

notes: Probe: /Users/miguel/.julia/dev/Redstone.jl/design/reports/20261124_doc_conformance/probes/L6c/probe.jl. It ran twice against W and its line numbers are the probe:N evidence. I changed no tracked file. All 30 entries carry Status ratified. Every D-nnn cited in a Position resolves to an entry with a link definition. The chains run D-166 -> D-263, D-271 -> D-276, D-435 -> D-438 and D-436 -> D-437, and each ends at a ratified entry. D-012's in-Position supersession by D-245 is ratified, and so are D-316's superseded entries D-060, D-255 and D-261. Every § link anchor used in log.md resolves to a spec.md heading slug. Policy on renamed identifiers: per log_rules.md rule 2, a renamed spelling with a recorded rename entry is old vocabulary, marked ok with the current name. This covers h_x/h_xu/h_z/h_zu, y_xu/y_z/y_zu and f/g (renamed by D-173/D-195/D-220/D-267), output_types (D-267), fragment's inputs keyword (set's u, log.md:12703), faces(...) (input_passthrough, D-144/D-171), project (x_projection) and Redstone.Blocks (Redstone.Library, D-453). Rules that the code contradicts and a later entry moved are findings of class drift. Four of them are already annotated inside their own entry, and their fix says so: D-100 (log.md:3404), D-137 (log.md:5009), D-237 (log.md:9755) and the D-035 rationale (log.md:1334). The StopRequest port-name finding (L6c-144) contradicts that entry's own 2026-11-12 annotation, which says the rest stands. SampleTerrainField, SimpleAtmosphere, atmospheric_field, T_sl, p_sl, q_eb and ω_eb_b are placeholders. integrator is a local example name, and unlisted is a rejected alternative absent from src. flag and request are finding L6c-144.
